core_summary: Covers practical geometry using an unmarked ruler and compass. It guides students through constructing perpendicular bisectors, right angles (90°), angle bisectors, copying angles, parallel lines, regular polygons (equilateral triangles, squares, regular hexagons), pointed arches, curved symmetric designs ('Eyes'), and introduces grid tiling (tessellations) without gaps or overlaps.
key_concepts: Construction using Unmarked Ruler and Compass
Construction of Perpendicular Bisectors and Segment Midpoints
Right Angle Construction (90°) and Angle Bisection
Copying Angles and Constructing Parallel Lines
Special Angles (60°, 120°) and Regular Hexagon Constructions
Curved Symmetric Designs and Pointed Arches via Supporting Lines
Tiling (Tessellation) of Grids using Repeating Shapes without gaps or overlaps

key_terms.definition: Drawing precise lines, angles, and shapes using only an unmarked straightedge ruler and a compass.
A line that divides a line segment into two equal segments at a 90° right angle.
Dividing a geometric entity (line segment or angle) into two equal parts.
A closed 2D polygon with all sides equal in length and all interior angles equal in measure.
Covering a two-dimensional region completely using repeating geometric shapes with no gaps and no overlaps.
A dissection puzzle consisting of seven flat polygon pieces arranged to form shapes.

key_takeaways: Geometrical constructions rely on fundamental properties of circles, equal radii, and triangle congruence conditions.
Every point on a perpendicular bisector is equidistant from the endpoints of the line segment.
Artistic and architectural figures (arches, rosettes) are systematically built using underlying supporting lines and arcs.
Shapes whose interior angles fit evenly around 360° can tile a plane seamlessly without gaps or overlaps.
